title: Rosemary's Baby
synopsis: A new apartment in an old building, neighbors who help too much, a tannis root necklace, and a husband who has been making promises behind a wall.

nodes.text: Bramford. High ceilings. A secretary cabinet shoved in front of a closet.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Take the place.” The story records the instinct as “Brave” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Pass” back. Wise shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: An old friend warns you about the building's history.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Listen.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Polite.

nodes.text: Behind the cabinet, a door, a smell, a board with a name on it.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Investigate” back. Curious shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: A young woman in the laundry room with a tannis root pendant.

choices.consequence: “Befriend her” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Heart.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Polite.

nodes.text: Terry's body in a pool of blood under the awning.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honest.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Cold—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: You sit by the cradle and you decide what to be his mother of. The strangers exchange a glance. It is, surprisingly, your house now.
You wrap a coat around the bassinet and walk out into Central Park West. The cult does not stop you. They never could.
Hill comes himself this time, with two policemen and an ambulance. The cult scatters. You spend a decade telling the story to people who do not believe you.
